Short version: 

- Great graphics. Characters look cool, except the females who basically look like males with moobs.
- Lots of weapons and weapons have special abilities. 
- Different weapons scale different ways just like in Dark Souls. 
- Good learning curve. You'll die when you get to new areas, which is expected in a souls-like game, but there are strategies to get around the new obstacles. 
- Mistakes are punishing and force you to pay attention. You need to learn to dodge.
- Watch out for melee attacks. It may seem strange but they hit SIGNIFICANTLY harder than the gunshots from most enemies. 
- A little clunky when it comes to the movement. Keep in mind that fall damage insta-kills you if it's more than 1 story high, even by like 1 foot. 
- Limited ammo, which is actually kind of a good thing. It teaches you to play sparingly, but you do typically have plenty to get through each area. There are consumables to refill it, too. 
- Weapon upgrade system works like Dark Souls, but you can upgrade at every obelisk (bonfire).

I bought this 50% off. Even so, I'd say the game is worth more than that. This game is filling my souls-like game craving for now.

- Good enough for its price

- Could use more different weak points for enemies

- Repeating bosses

- Non-exixtance AI (Most bosses just stand there and shoot you, never moves)

- Hope it undergo the same process of Lords of the Fallen > The Surge, if it does the next game is goanna be good.

Picked it up on sale and so far impressed;
Very Dark Souls-esque, pretty difficult but not to a point where you feel like you aren't progressing, say a learning curve on every different enemy/boss, rewarding when you succeed. Plenty of exploration and hidden areas for rewards, and very good lore/story.

On the downside; you get frame drops in a few select areas (albeit rarely) but not to a point where it's unplayable.
There's very little guidance right from the start; areas aren't mapped and can occasionally be difficult to navigate.

Definitely worth giving it a go, all the fundementals are there and most issues can be easily addressed in time as the game gets older.

I have mixed feelings about this game, while I enjoyed like the first 3 hours of it the rest of the game was boring and repetitive.

As part of the ultra-hardcore action RPG such as dark souls you should expect more than challenge from that genre however while you approach to the conclusion of the game and specially the final 3/2 acts this game more than a challenge becomes a broken unplayable ♥♥♥♥, dark souls sure is a hard challenge but at least you have the tools to defeat and overcome all enemies, in here once you get knocked you are dead.

Enemies coming out of nowhere dragon ball style and knocking you down make impossible to enjoy the game you dont even have the chance to enjoy it and by the end is just repetitive and boring, is just wave after wave of enemies in maps that do not change at all whatsoever and look just the same.

The melee combat is clunky, you literally perform the same two moves with all melee weapons, crafting materials even the more simple ones are very rare to find, same goes for your "bits" the principal currency for leveling up your character this makes progression a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ grind and just almost nonexistent.

No character customization at all, guns of the same type feel and shoot exactly the same just with different stats.

Game has its issues, its not perfect but its not horrible either. Devs are constantly checking the comments and updating the game, its good to know that they care. AI can be a little finiky sometimes but most of the time its doing what it should and thats make your time really difficult. If you like hardcore games and want to sink hours getting lost, stumbing upon bosses, running your face into them until theyre dead and upgrading yourself to become shy of a tank, give it a go.

A less polished Dark Souls  focused on guns that asks a high entry fee normally; I picked this up at half off and that tempers my annoyance with it but still doesn't make it a game I'd recommend at half off. Even after learning the mechanics and the movements of various enemies, I found a major problem with general gameplay after the November 19th patch which added stat diversity for equipping weapons. Here is my problem with this and thus the game, and one I imagine does go away as you struggle and claw through to higher levels so you can equip any new weapons:

The beginning of the game will throw a slew of various wepaonry at you that you may want to try to see if you like the playstyle. However, you won't be able to do that because all the weapons you get will require a substantial investment even in the early hours of the game to be able to equip them. This also typically means you're not able to invest in things like heatlh to just have the HP to survive an extra hit or two because you're desperately trying to get enough strength to equip a grenade launcher, a stat which you'll also need for your laughably bad early melee weapons and occasionally random other weapons classified as heavy. But first you'll want an endless amount of stamina/endurance to be able to constantly rush up to enemies, dodge behind them, and hit the only spot where they will take reasonable amounts of damage not coated in ten inches of unobtanium powermech Spetsnaz anti-all-your-weapons armor. And you're going to want to have a massive stat spread to be able to equip different elemental damage weapons that some enemies that are tough might otherwise be weak to, but you'l llikely have to spend hours in the early levels grinding garbage mobs to get a few stat points for that. Further along this path, you're going to try to focus on equipping this new item you got, put all your stats into the one spot you need, and then loot a better version of that item which takes entirely different stats.

This all said, there's a basis for good things in this game and patching could address my issues and others that people have brought up with the game. Continued support from the creators could smooth rough edges enough to make it a good souls-like, though I don't see that as it's made now it has potential to be a great one.

First, don't let the haters of the Souls-Like genre fool you. They're all just jaded bc of Dark Souls. 

This game is not Dark Souls. It is similar, but it's a third-person shooter, with minimal melee. It's not very balanced, but it's not broken. It's not an amazing game and it is fairly repetitive once you catch on to giant elephant of a weak-spot that 90% of the enemies have. Basically you'll just spend a giant portion of your time dodging behind an enemy to hit that big red button that says, "Pls Kill Me Now." And most of the bosses are pretty similar in that regard.

That being said, sniper Rifles are op AF. IMHO, they are very unbalanced compared to the rest of the weapons. They will kill anything VERY quickly if you shoot it in the head or lock-on, dodge-roll and shoot it in the back for the "EZPZ killshot." Most other weapons are pretty trash compared to the sniper rifles in terms of raw damage output. So, if you want to make it EZ on yourself, L2-Lockon Stratos and it's like, GG - Sniping is so EZ!

Again, don't let the negative reviews fool you. This game is a good game. Not bad, but not great. Get it on a good sale.

My two favourite genres of games are ARPGs and 3rd person shooters, so this game seemed like a match made in heaven. Unfortunately it is marred by a couple of design decisions which ultimately meant it was not for me.

Firstly I found that I wasn’t doing much damage with my weapons, even with headshots, and it was after a while I realised all of the enemies have weak points on their back to facilitate quick killing. Unfortunately there is only way to expose most of them and that is to bait an attack, dodge it and then get a few shots away. Then I discovered you don’t actually have to aim as you can lock on by pressing the right stick. So you end up locking on, waiting for an enemy to approach, bait an attack, dodge, and then counter. At this point I realised I was basically playing a far less polished Dark Souls, and was doing minimal Third Person Shooting.

Not for me at this stage. If the enemies had more varied weak spots, some that were best tackled at range and some up close that would help alleviate the problem, but I felt very disincentivized to engage with the free aiming and shooting when the most effective means of killing enemies was to basically play it like dark souls and forgo the range benefit of having a gun.

Aiming also doesn’t feel quite right on a controller, there is almost some momentum to it, so when you release the control stick the cursor takes a small amount of time to ‘decelerate’.

My characters animations were also very ‘jittery’ when turning in small increments which was very annoying when everything else is moving very smoothly.

I may end up giving this another go in the future, maybe when it is a tad cheaper as even on sale, this game is competing with some heavy hitters at this price point.
